- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates upside; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean to compensate for suppressed volatility.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid false optimism.  
- If recent auction supply is high (e.g., CAP3 EU or DE), model tends to overreact; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon after volatility spikes; if forecast is >15% above recent 10d average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint (e.g., if 10/18 days bullish, forecast 10% above mean).
